question: Decision (EU) 2021/991 authorises France, by way of derogation from Articles 28, 30 and 110 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), to impose lower taxes on local products than on imported products. This measure is limited to the products listed in Annex I of the decision.

However, dock dues are levied on imports of almost all goods, including products for which there is no local production subject to internal dock dues, such as tyres in Guadeloupe. More than 96 % of its revenue comes from imports. 1.

On what legal basis does the Commission consider dock dues levied on imports of products with no local production to constitute internal taxation within the meaning of Article 110 TFEU, not a charge having equivalent effect to a customs duty?
Has it assessed, as part of its proposal COM(2026)0662, the share of revenue from dock dues levied on products for which there is no local production, and its impact on consumer prices?
Does it intend to ask France to provide it with that data before the Council of the European Union adopts the decision?
